evidence: The trip starts at SH73 on the true right of the Waimakariri River, just south of the Bealey road bridge (about 10 km east of Arthur's Pass village).
The route follows O'Malley's Track for the first stage of the trip.
Leave SH73 on the true right of the Waimakariri River, immediately south of the road bridge over the river.
Just before the White River joins the Waimakariri River, a short section of marked track leads to Carrington Hut, marked by a large rock cairn and orange marker.

evidence: A 2 km long gravel road leads to the Waimakariri riverbed from the western side of Klondyke Corner.
The quickest way to Carrington Hut is to head straight up the Waimakariri valley from this point, cutting corners and crossing the river where necessary.
Follow the marked track to Carrington Hut

doubts: Start ref F1 is the only road end (an unnamed track meeting West Coast Road); the text calls the road SH73, so F1 is taken as that start on the Bealey bridge side, but the packet does not name SH73 as West Coast Road. The original SH73 – Carrington Hut track is cut off 2 km upstream from Anti Crow Hut and needs river crossings; the main way's via is as described. O'Malley's Track has no map entry. The riverbed route (W2) starts from a 2 km gravel road off the western side of Klondyke Corner; the exact start point is the road's riverbed end, not Klondyke Corner itself.
